newsitem.title: CHINA: Sundiro H1 output seen up 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sundiro H1 output seen up 50 pct.

text.p: China's Hainan Sundiro Motorcycle Co Ltd, which is preparing for a B share initial public offering, said on Thursday first-half 1997 motorcycle output had grown a year-on-year 50 percent.
Production jumped to 230,000 units in the first half of 1997 from 153,000 in the year-ago period, a company spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securiites Bulletin.
The higher output was due to successful technological upgrades which resulted in expanded production capacity, he said.
Sundiro, based in Haikou, capital of the island province of Hainan, produced 350,000 motorcycles in 1996.
The company expected to issue of 150 million B shares in October this year for listing in Shenzhen, the official said.
Sundiro has said it would use part of the proceeds to upgrade production technology and set up a venture with Japanese firm Kawasaki to make motorbike engines.
Sundiro has named China Cinda Trust and Investment Corp as the domestic chief underwriter and ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett as the international coordinator, another Sundiro official said last month.
Sundiro posted net profits of 219.0 million yuan in 1996 against 70.55 million yuan in 1995 based on Chinese accounting standards.
The spokesman declined to give an estimated profit figure for 1997.
Sundiro, one of the 33 companies selected by Beijing as a new batch of firms to issue B shares, had a 1997 production target of 600,000 to 800,000 motorcycles, he said.
At the end of 1996, Sundiro had about 237 million outstanding shares, composed of 142 million institutional shares, 95 million A shares and 72,240 staff shares.
